findings.text: the plan's §3 capability "Scope a run to a release batch" (docs/plans/sn-catalog-audit-instrument.html:399) proposes a new manifest-scoped selector to read west_production_dd_paths.yaml, but resolve_batch_token (sources_manifest.py:81), load_focus_file (:183) and load_sources_file (:113) already resolve that manifest and its kind, and graph_ops.scope_exact_standard_names (imas_codex/standard_names/graph_ops.py:2004) already binds an exact identity set from source paths — so the selector forks an owner that exists

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is added; each of the four capabilities extends an existing one instead of fanning into wrappers (pipeline.py, enrichment.py, cli/sn.py), and the one import across a boundary (harmonize.build_worklist) replaces behaviour rather than re-laying it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements manifest-to-scope resolution that imas_codex/standard_names/sources_manifest.py already owns and that three call sites on `sn run` already use.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; the release-batch selector section adds a CLI option and its own text names nothing it retires or merges, nor why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites harmonize.py, the compose-path comparator collector it reuses, and the review templates, but never searched the manifest-scope machinery that already resolves the exact file it names, so it proposes a new selector beside the owner.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the one added surface, `--target groups`, is a branch on the existing `sn review` command over harmonize.build_worklist, and the plan states why the module cannot be reached otherwise (it has no CLI surface) rather than adding a parallel `sn harmonize`.
